title: Symbol
primary_statement: an element of a fixed countable alphabet

title: String
primary_statement: a finite sequence of symbols

title: Finite sequence
primary_statement: a finite list of objects of one type

title: Inductive definition
primary_statement: a set given by base and closure clauses, with induction and recursion principles

title: Metatheoretic induction
primary_statement: ordinary and strong induction and recursion on the metatheoretic natural numbers

title: Naive collection
primary_statement: informal set-of talk used only in semantic nodes; discharged from above by the set capsule

title: Well-formed propositional formula
primary_statement: atoms closed under the connectives by an inductive definition

title: Verum and falsum
primary_statement: top as p to p; bottom primitive with ex falso

title: Formula complexity measures
primary_statement: length and connective-height of a wff, for induction

title: Unique readability
primary_statement: every wff has exactly one parse; licenses recursion on structure

title: Subformula
primary_statement: the nodes of a wffs parse tree

title: Structural induction on wffs
primary_statement: a property holding of atoms and preserved by each connective holds of every wff

title: Recursion on wff structure
primary_statement: a function on wffs is determined by its atom values and one clause per connective

title: Truth assignment
primary_statement: a function from atoms to true or false

title: Truth-value recursion
primary_statement: the value of a wff under an assignment, by recursion on structure

title: Satisfaction (propositional)
primary_statement: v satisfies phi when the truth-value recursion gives true

title: Truth table
primary_statement: the finite tabulation of a wffs value over all assignments to its atoms

title: Tautology
primary_statement: true under every truth assignment

title: Contradiction
primary_statement: false under every truth assignment

title: Satisfiability
primary_statement: true under at least one truth assignment

title: Semantic consequence (propositional)
primary_statement: every assignment satisfying all of Gamma satisfies phi

title: Logical equivalence
primary_statement: mutual semantic consequence; same truth value under every assignment

title: Substitution of equivalents
primary_statement: replacing a subformula by an equivalent one preserves equivalence

title: Duality principle
primary_statement: swapping and-or and true-false and negating atoms negates a wff

title: Decidability of tautology
primary_statement: whether a wff is a tautology is decided by its finite truth table

title: Double negation
primary_statement: not not p is equivalent to p (classically)

title: De Morgan laws (propositional)
primary_statement: not (p and q) iff not p or not q ; not (p or q) iff not p and not q

title: Distributivity
primary_statement: and over or and or over and

title: Implication as disjunction
primary_statement: p to q is equivalent to not p or q (classically)

title: Contraposition
primary_statement: p to q is equivalent to not q to not p

title: Biconditional decomposition
primary_statement: p iff q is (p to q) and (q to p)

title: Commutativity, associativity, idempotence
primary_statement: and and or are commutative, associative, idempotent

title: Absorption
primary_statement: p and (p or q) is p ; p or (p and q) is p

title: Exportation
primary_statement: (p and q) to r is equivalent to p to (q to r)

title: Negation normal form
primary_statement: every wff is equivalent to one with negation only on atoms

title: Conjunctive normal form
primary_statement: every wff is equivalent to a conjunction of clauses

title: Disjunctive normal form
primary_statement: every wff is equivalent to a disjunction of terms

title: DNF from the truth table
primary_statement: the rows evaluating to true give an explicit equivalent DNF

title: Functional completeness
primary_statement: not-and-or expresses every Boolean function

title: Sheffer and Peirce
primary_statement: nand alone, and nor alone, are each functionally complete

title: The sixteen binary connectives
primary_statement: there are exactly sixteen functions from two bits to one bit

title: Natural-deduction derivation
primary_statement: a finite tree of wffs with discharged assumptions

title: Propositional ND rules
primary_statement: introduction and elimination rules for each connective, plus bottom-elimination

title: Assumption discharge
primary_statement: an implication-introduction closes off a temporarily assumed wff

title: Reductio ad absurdum
primary_statement: from a derivation of bottom under not phi, conclude phi (classical rule)

title: Ex falso quodlibet
primary_statement: from bottom, derive any wff (intuitionistic)

title: Hilbert system (propositional)
primary_statement: three axiom schemas and modus ponens

title: Modus ponens
primary_statement: from phi and phi to psi, infer psi

title: Hilbert derivation
primary_statement: a finite sequence of wffs, each an axiom instance or an MP consequence

title: Derivability
primary_statement: Gamma proves phi in the calculus; calculus-independent after the equivalence lemma

title: Deduction theorem
primary_statement: Gamma with phi proves psi iff Gamma proves phi to psi

title: ND and Hilbert coincide
primary_statement: the same wffs are derivable in the ND and Hilbert calculi

title: Derived rules
primary_statement: modus tollens, disjunctive syllogism, cut, and others are admissible

title: Consistency
primary_statement: Gamma is consistent when it does not prove bottom

title: Soundness (propositional)
primary_statement: if Gamma proves phi then Gamma semantically entails phi

title: Maximal consistent set
primary_statement: a consistent set of wffs with no consistent proper extension

title: Lindenbaum's lemma (propositional)
primary_statement: every consistent set extends to a maximal consistent set

title: Truth lemma (propositional)
primary_statement: a maximal consistent set induces an assignment satisfying exactly its members

title: Post completeness theorem
primary_statement: if Gamma semantically entails phi then Gamma proves phi

title: Compactness (propositional)
primary_statement: a set of wffs is satisfiable iff every finite subset is

title: Signature (first-order language)
primary_statement: constant, function, and relation symbols with arities, plus logical equality

title: Terms
primary_statement: variables and constants closed under function-symbol application

title: Atomic formula
primary_statement: a relation symbol or equality applied to terms

title: Quantifiers
primary_statement: for-all and there-exists binding a variable in a wff

title: First-order well-formed formula
primary_statement: atomic formulas closed under connectives and quantifiers

title: Free and bound variables
primary_statement: an occurrence is bound if under a quantifier on that variable, else free

title: Sentence
primary_statement: a wff with no free variables

title: Substitution
primary_statement: replace every free occurrence of a variable by a term

title: Free for (no capture)
primary_statement: t is free for x in phi when no free variable of t is captured by a quantifier of phi

title: Alpha-equivalence
primary_statement: renaming bound variables gives a logically interchangeable wff

title: Prenex normal form
primary_statement: every wff is equivalent to one with all quantifiers in front

title: Structure
primary_statement: a nonempty domain with interpretations of every non-logical symbol

title: Variable assignment
primary_statement: a function from variables to domain elements, with pointwise update

title: Term evaluation
primary_statement: the domain element denoted by a term under an assignment, by recursion

title: Tarski satisfaction
primary_statement: structure satisfies wff under assignment, by recursion including the quantifier clauses

title: Model
primary_statement: a structure satisfying every sentence of a set

title: Validity
primary_statement: true in every structure under every assignment

title: Semantic consequence (first-order)
primary_statement: every model of Gamma under every assignment satisfies phi

title: Coincidence lemma
primary_statement: satisfaction depends only on the assignment to the free variables

title: Substitution lemma (semantic)
primary_statement: satisfying phi with t substituted equals satisfying phi under the updated assignment

title: First-order logic with equality
primary_statement: equality is logical and always interpreted as identity on the domain

title: Equality is a congruence
primary_statement: equal elements are interchangeable in every relation and function

title: Negation of quantifiers
primary_statement: not for-all x phi iff there-exists x not phi ; not exists iff for-all not

title: Quantifier duality
primary_statement: there-exists x phi is equivalent to not for-all x not phi

title: Quantifier distribution
primary_statement: for-all distributes over and, there-exists over or; the other directions can fail

title: Quantifier order
primary_statement: exists y for-all x entails for-all x exists y, never the converse

title: Vacuous quantification
primary_statement: quantifying a variable not free in phi leaves phi equivalent (nonempty domain)

title: Quantifier ND rules
primary_statement: introduction and elimination rules for both quantifiers

title: Eigenvariable condition
primary_statement: the fresh variable in for-all-intro and exists-elim must not occur free in conclusion or open assumptions

title: Hilbert quantifier axioms
primary_statement: the for-all-instantiation schema and the generalization rule

title: Equality axioms
primary_statement: reflexivity and the substitution schema for equality

title: Derivability (first-order)
primary_statement: the first-order calculus proves phi from Gamma

title: Soundness (first-order)
primary_statement: if Gamma proves phi then Gamma semantically entails phi

title: Consistency (first-order)
primary_statement: a first-order theory that does not prove bottom

title: Henkin constants
primary_statement: add a witnessing constant for every existential wff, iterating over a chain of languages

title: Henkin theory
primary_statement: a maximal consistent theory with the witness property for every existential

title: Lindenbaum's lemma (first-order)
primary_statement: every consistent theory extends to a maximal consistent one

title: Term model
primary_statement: the structure whose domain is closed terms modulo provable equality

title: Truth lemma (first-order)
primary_statement: in the term model a sentence is true iff it is in the Henkin theory

title: Godel completeness theorem
primary_statement: every semantically valid consequence is derivable; every consistent theory has a model

title: Compactness (first-order)
primary_statement: a theory has a model iff every finite subset does

title: Downward Lowenheim-Skolem
primary_statement: a theory with an infinite model in a countable language has a countable model

title: Upward Lowenheim-Skolem
primary_statement: a theory with an infinite model has models of every larger cardinality

title: Skolem paradox
primary_statement: countable models of set theory exist; countability is not absolute

title: Non-categoricity
primary_statement: first-order theories with an infinite model are never categorical

title: Non-finite-axiomatizability
primary_statement: infinity, and many theories, cannot be captured by finitely many first-order axioms

title: Direct proof
primary_statement: assume the antecedent and derive the consequent by implication-introduction

title: Proof by contrapositive
primary_statement: prove not q to not p in place of p to q

title: Proof by contradiction
primary_statement: assume the negation, derive bottom, conclude (RAA)

title: Proof by cases
primary_statement: from an exhaustive disjunction, prove the goal under each disjunct (or-elimination)

title: Proof of a biconditional
primary_statement: prove both implications separately

title: Existence proof
primary_statement: constructive (exhibit a witness) versus pure-existence (non-constructive)

title: Uniqueness proof
primary_statement: assume two objects with the property and show they are equal

title: Disproof by counterexample
primary_statement: refute for-all x phi by exhibiting an x with not phi

title: Without loss of generality
primary_statement: reduce to a representative case justified by a symmetry

title: Weak induction
primary_statement: base case and successor step give the property for every natural number

title: Strong induction
primary_statement: the property for all predecessors gives it at n; equivalent to weak induction

title: Structural induction
primary_statement: induction along the clauses of any inductive definition

title: Well-ordering principle
primary_statement: every nonempty set of natural numbers has a least element

title: Induction principles coincide
primary_statement: weak induction, strong induction, and well-ordering are equivalent over the naturals

title: Vacuous and trivial proof
primary_statement: a false antecedent or a true consequent proves an implication outright

title: Decidability
primary_statement: a set is decidable when membership is settled by an always-halting procedure

title: Church-Turing thesis
primary_statement: the informally computable functions are exactly the Turing-computable ones

title: Undecidability of first-order validity
primary_statement: no algorithm decides whether an arbitrary first-order sentence is valid

title: Halting problem
primary_statement: no algorithm decides whether an arbitrary program halts on a given input

title: Godel first incompleteness theorem
primary_statement: any consistent recursively axiomatized theory interpreting arithmetic has an undecided sentence

title: Godel second incompleteness theorem
primary_statement: such a theory cannot prove its own consistency

title: Tarski undefinability of truth
primary_statement: arithmetical truth is not definable by an arithmetical formula

title: Incompleteness of PA and ZFC
primary_statement: if consistent and recursively axiomatized, PA and ZFC are incomplete

title: Logical equivalence (first-order)
primary_statement: mutual first-order semantic consequence
